transcript: In To Free a Mockingbird, Grace Aki weaves a tapestry of anecdotes from her and her family's history, in all its comedic and tragic glory. This solo show flows a lot like a stand upset with Grace inundating you with jokes at breakneck speed while delicately navigating and maximizing the tonal shifts that make this piece as devastating as it is funny. Many of the dark aspects get deliberately glossed over, which makes for great irony and leaves room for the heavy moments that she does face head-on to breathe. There's a lot packed into this show, so much that you may not be able to keep all of it straight afterwards, but you'll almost certainly remember Grace's charismatic and humorous delivery of it. In what sometimes feels like an endless sea of solo pieces, I think this one offers something uniquely captivating in its earnest but matter-of-fact treatment of potent material. To Free a Mockingbird is running at Soho Playhouse through this Sunday.
